candidates.reason: Coupon spectra do not automatically equal finite-device response when thickness, domains, q dependence and zero-frequency limits compete.

lostStructure: Uniform control of thickness, lateral size, q to zero and frequency to zero limits.

candidates.reopeningTrigger: A finite-geometry response calculation with measured nonlocal/thickness corrections and declared order of limits.

candidates.reason: Causality, Kramers-Kronig consistency, passivity and Onsager/reversal constraints are the invariant checks that make the cross-channel tensor meaningful.

lostStructure: They do not fix numerical oscillator strengths or magnetic-domain populations.

candidates.reopeningTrigger: A same-film channel violating the frozen invariant ledger outside full calibration covariance.

candidates.reason: EX-012 explicitly maps raw transport, ellipsometric and magneto-optic records into one tensor and tests held-out channels without force-data refitting.

candidates.reopeningTrigger: The EX-012 cross-channel detector closure passes its preregistered held-out and covariance gates.

candidates.reason: The tensor must be causal and passive in the measured state, but equilibrium/KMS use in Lifshitz theory additionally requires controlled temperature, stationarity and material state.

lostStructure: Nonequilibrium domain kinetics and preparation-history dependence.

candidates.reopeningTrigger: Temperature- and history-stable same-film response satisfying passivity and equilibrium consistency across the required band.

candidates.reason: Optical-tail freedom, magnetic domains, thickness variation and cross-channel calibration can reproduce partial tensor records and are explicit EX-012 nulls.
